{"op":"set_pin","component":"M6","pin":"Drain","net":"n6","why":"M6 is diode-connected and its drain feeds only the next stack device, not the shared output net"},
{"op":"set_pin","component":"M6","pin":"Gate","net":"n6"},
{"op":"set_pin","component":"M10","pin":"Source","net":"n6"},
{"op":"set_pin","component":"M10","pin":"Drain","net":"n7d","why":"the stack bottom device drain joins the drain of the NMOS below it, not the bias line"},
{"op":"set_pin","component":"M12","pin":"Drain","net":"n7d"},
{"op":"set_pin","component":"M10","pin":"Gate","net":"g13","why":"this gate runs along y=250 to the gate of the compensation transistor"},
{"op":"set_pin","component":"M9","pin":"Gate","net":"g13"},
{"op":"set_pin","component":"M7","pin":"Source","net":"tail","why":"input-pair sources and the tail transistor drain form the tail net"},
{"op":"set_pin","component":"M8","pin":"Source","net":"tail"},
{"op":"set_pin","component":"M15","pin":"Drain","net":"tail"},
{"op":"set_pin","component":"M15","pin":"Gate","net":"net9","why":"bias bus along the bottom"},
{"op":"set_pin","component":"M13","pin":"Gate","net":"net9"},
{"op":"set_pin","component":"M14","pin":"Gate","net":"net9"},
{"op":"remove_pin","component":"M12","pin":"Body"},
{"op":"remove_pin","component":"M13","pin":"Body"},
{"op":"remove_pin","component":"M15","pin":"Body"},
{"op":"set_pin","component":"M4","pin":"Gate","net":"net4","why":"mirror gate line is shared with the other top PMOS gates"},
{"op":"remove_pin","component":"M5","pin":"Body"}
]}

I'm working through how the pipeline's components map onto the circuit in the image. I'm still tracing where the drains and gates of that load connect down to the output stage.

Now I'm mapping the pipeline's components onto the actual circuit: M1 through M5 correspond to image M5, M4, M14, M11, and M3, with M5 apparently gate-tied to its drain. I'm still checking the stack of M5, M6, and M7 on the left, which looks like a bias chain feeding a current source.

I'm checking the remaining pipeline components against the image's labels, and the mapping keeps shifting, so I'm going through each device's bounding box and type one at a time. The input pair looks like it should be NMOS rather than PMOS, and I still need to confirm which image devices they correspond to.

I'm now checking the remaining pipeline components against the image, starting with the NMOS input devices and the M13 compensation transistor at the bottom. For M13 I'm looking at whether it's PMOS, since its body arrow points up, and at how its gate and drain nets are tied to the rest of the circuit. The netlist nets look heavily merged, with net6 seeming to pick up M3's gate as well.

I'm now working out the correct nets for the image's M5 and M6 stack, since the pipeline has them all merged into one node. I'll redo the true connectivity using the pipeline's component names.

Now I'm tracing the connections for the image's M6 and M7 stack: M6's source ties to M5's drain, and it's diode-connected with its drain feeding M7's source. I still need to pin down what M7's gate and drain connect to.

Now I'm tracing the connections for the M7 gate, which seems to run along a horizontal wire toward the M13 region, though that link is hard to confirm from the image.

The gate of M7 seems to run along a wire toward the bias node feeding M13, so it may not be tied to its own drain the way M6 is.

I'm checking where the drain of M7 meets the bottom bus, with dots at 115,268 and 165,268, and whether M9's drain runs up to that junction. The image's M9 gate also looks like it ties into that same bus.

I'm checking the bias bus and the M8 diode at the bottom, then tracing M9, whose gate sits on that bus and whose drain meets the M7 drain at the junction near (115,268) and (165,268), so it sinks the stack current to ground. M7's gate, though, runs along the wire at y≈250 toward M13's gate, not back to its own drain.

I'm fixing the pipeline's net assignments for the M10 and M12 drains, and I'm tying M10's gate to the M13 gate net. I'm also checking that M13's terminals match the image: the left one joins the M12 drain line at x=400 and the right one goes to Cc.

Now I'm checking the top PMOS pair: the image's M4 is diode-connected with its gate on its drain, sourced from VDD, and the net shared with the image M2 drain looks right as it stands. I'm moving on to the image M3, whose drain should sit on the same node as the image M1 drain and the M11 gate, which is where the merged net needs correcting.

Now I'm checking the M3 drain node: it runs down to the M1 drain and across toward the M11 gate, so M4's gate in the pipeline should sit on that node rather than on net7. The pipeline's drain assignment for M4 also looks wrong, so I'm correcting both the gate and drain nets there.

I'm checking the node at the top of the first stage: the M3 and M1 drains meet there, and it looks like it should drive the M14 gate, with the M11 gate hanging off the same line.

I'm guessing M11 might be a current mirror copying M4, since its gate seems tied to the M3/M4 gate line, though the wire from 258 doesn't clearly reach it.

I'm checking whether M11's gate might share the M4 gate net, which would make it a mirror, though the wiring doesn't settle that. The pipeline lists M4 with its drain on net6 and its gate on net7, and that gate assignment looks wrong to me.

I'm checking whether the wire running from the M3 body at about x=318 actually reaches the M11 gate near x=376, which would tie M11's gate to the first-stage node. The picture is hard to read at that spot, so I'm not sure yet whether that line goes all the way across.

I'm still trying to pin down whether M11's gate lands on the M3 drain node or on the M4 gate net, since the body wire near x≈318 might tie it to the first-stage output. The M14 gate line at y≈140 could also join that same node, which would make the drains common, so I'm weighing whether M11 is meant to be a mirror.

Still weighing whether M11's gate lands on the first-stage output or on the M4 gate net, and whether the y≈140 wire ties M3's drain to M14's gate; if so, the first-stage node should drive M14's gate, with M3's drain, M1's drain, and M11's gate on it.

I'm checking where the M14 gate connects: the line at y≈140 might tie the M11 drain node to M14's gate, and I'm trying to confirm whether there's a junction dot at (400,140) or (315,140).

I'm still trying to tell whether the M11 gate sits on the M3 drain node or on the M4 gate net, since the wire near the M3 body looks like it runs across the top toward M11. The picture doesn't make that clear, so I'm not settling it yet.

I'm weighing whether M11 is a current mirror of M4, copying its gate net, which would make its drain feed the node at x≈400 and bias the M14 gate. The pipeline's body-net assignment at (318,92) also needs checking against that picture, but I don't want to settle it from the wiring alone.

I'm going to treat the M11 gate as net4, since the wire from the M3 body may just be the mirror gate line continuing across. That would put M11 in a current-mirror arrangement with M4, with its drain landing on the node at x≈400 that feeds M12 and M13.

I'm settling on the first-stage output as the node at x≈315, joined across y≈140 to x≈400 and then to the M14 gate. If the junction at (400,140) is merged, M11's drain feeds the same node, and M11 acts as a current source into it.

I'm settling on the merged node at x≈400 as the first-stage output, tying M3's drain, M11's drain, and M14's gate together. The pipeline's net assignments for M3, M4, M5, M8, M9, M13 and M15 mostly sit on that same node, so I'm tracing where the drain junctions actually land before fixing the remaining labels.

Now I'm settling on the net assignments: the tail node joins M7's source, M8's source, and M15's drain, while the first-stage output carries M3's gate, M4 and M5 drains, M8 and M9 drains, and M13's drain. I'm still unsure whether M4's gate should be merged onto the M11 gate net, so I'm leaving that open for now.

I'm assigning the tail net to M7's source, M8's source, and M15's drain, and giving M6's drain and gate and M10's source a new node. M10's drain and M12's drain would share another new node, with M10's gate tied to the g13 net.

Now I'm settling the remaining labels: M9's gate joins the g13 net along with M10's gate, and M15's gate stays with the M12 gate net.

Now I'm mapping the bias bus, where the M11 and M12 gates should all sit on net9. The M15 gate, the M13 gate, and the M14 gate currently point at separate nets, so those get merged into net9 too.

Next I'm clearing out the body pins on M12, M13, and M15 so the leftover body nets don't dangle once their gates move onto the bias bus.

Next I'm setting M12's gate to the bias bus and moving its drain onto the n7d node, then checking M9's gate, which moves onto the g13 net. The M14 drain stays on the output net with its source on ground, and the M15 drain stays on the tail while its gate joins the bias bus. Last, I'm dropping the M5 body pin on the leftover net7 now that the M4 gate has moved off it.

Now I'm settling the leftover body pins, since M6 and M10 are fine as they are and the edit list is nearly done.
